informal: The Lean proves fourth-root norm estimates for the estimator: importance reweighting changes the conditioning slice exactly, the clipped relative error of a sample term costs \((b/a)^{1/4}\) or \((b/a)^{3/4}\) times the child root discrepancy, a wholly fine tail costs \((b/a)^{3/4}\), increments are enumerated by \(O(d)\)-bit descriptors, and mean prefixes and walk noise of the additive schedule meet their precision bounds.

results.informal: Multiplying the conditional mean of an array supported on \(Y_{a'}\) by \(\pi_a/\pi_{a'}\) gives its conditional mean on the narrower slice, so a carried bin term has conditional mean \((\rho_k/\rho_a)\,\mathbb E[f\mid\mathcal C^{u,\max(a,k)}]\).
results.note: mean_move is the conditioning-change identity \(\mathbb E[\frac{\pi_a}{\pi_b}\mathbf 1_{Y_b}V\mid\mathcal C^{u,a}]=\mathbb E[V\mid\mathcal C^{u,b}]\) at the core of the proof and carry_change applies it to a carried term; the full statement for all formulas is not one Lean lemma.

decls.name: mean_move
decls.informal: If \(a\le a'\) and \(f\) is supported on the terminal slice \(Y_{a'}\), then for \(j\in S\), \(\frac{\pi_a}{\pi_{a'}}\,\mathbb E[f_{ij}\mid\mathcal C^{u,a}_{ij}]=\mathbb E[f_{ij}\mid\mathcal C^{u,a'}_{ij}]\).

chunks.EstimatorBounds.mean_move/0: The masking identity for the narrower slice, with \(f=\mathbf 1_{Y_{a'}}f\), relates the two conditional means.
chunks.EstimatorBounds.mean_move/1: Clearing the denominator \(\pi_{a'}>0\) gives the identity.

decls.name: carry_change
decls.informal: If \(f\) is supported on \(Y_{\max(a,k)}\), then for \(j\in S\), \(\mathbb E[\text{carry}_k f\mid\mathcal C^{u,a}]_{ij}=\frac{\rho_k}{\rho_a}\,\mathbb E[f\mid\mathcal C^{u,\max(a,k)}]_{ij}\).

results.informal: The fourth-root difference contracts under nonnegative mixtures, and \(0\le s\le Cu\) with \(C\ge1\) implies \(\min\{1,|s-t|/(1+u)\}\le32C\,|s^{1/4}-t^{1/4}|\).
results.note: With \(s=4\) the Lean works directly with \(|H^{1/4}-H'^{1/4}|\), which the paper shows comparable to \(\mathcal L\), and proves its mixture contraction and the \(a=1\) form of the relative-loss inequality; \(\mathcal L\) itself is not defined.

decls.name: mixtures
decls.informal: For a nonnegative integral \(\mathcal I\) and \(f,g\ge0\), \((\mathcal I(f)^{1/4}-\mathcal I(g)^{1/4})^4\le\mathcal I\big((f^{1/4}-g^{1/4})^4\big)\).

chunks.AffineSampling.mixtures/0: Write \(\mathcal I(f)^{1/4}=\|f^{1/4}\|_{L_4(\mathcal I)}\), likewise for \(g\), and set \(f'=f^{1/4}\), \(g'=g^{1/4}\).
chunks.AffineSampling.mixtures/2: Raising to the fourth power preserves this inequality.
chunks.AffineSampling.mixtures/3: Since \(\|h\|_{L_4}^4=\mathcal I(h^4)\), this is the claim.

chunks.AffineSampling.fidelity/5: If \(|v-w|\ge1\), the left side is at most \(1\le32C|v-w|\).
chunks.AffineSampling.fidelity/6: If \(|v-w|\le1\), the clipped error is again at most \(32C|v-w|\).

results.informal: The \(L_4\) norm of the clipped relative error of a carried first-channel mean is at most \(64K^4\sigma(a,k)\) times the child root discrepancy, with \(\sigma=2^{a-k}\) for coarse and \(2^{-3(k-a)}\) for fine bins, and changing the endpoint scale of a deterministic array costs \(2\cdot2^{a'-a}\).
results.note: With \(s=4\) and \(b/a=\rho_k/\rho_a=2^{4(a-k)}\), \(\sigma\) equals \((b/a)^{1/4}\) or \((b/a)^{3/4}\), the fourth roots of the paper's costs \(b/a\) and \((b/a)^{s-1}\); the source-release factor \(f/u\) is handled by other lemmas.

decls.name: stream_fee
decls.informal: Assume \(2^{\max(a,k)}\le n\), \(K\ge1\), \(f,g\) have fourth roots in \([0,K]\) and are supported on \(Y_{\max(a,k)}\), \(D\ge0\), and \(\bar f_{ij}\le KD_{ij}\) where \(\bar h=\mathbb E[\text{carry}_k h\mid\mathcal C^{u,a}]\); then \(\big\|\min\{1,|\bar f-\bar g|/(1+D)\}\big\|_{u,a;4}\le64K^4\,\sigma(a,k)\,\|f^{1/4}-g^{1/4}\|_{u,\max(a,k);4}\), with \(\sigma(a,k)=2^{a-k}\) if \(k\le a\) and \(2^{-3(k-a)}\) otherwise.

chunks.EstimatorBounds.stream_fee/1: Each clipped relative error \(\min\{1,|v_{ij}|/(1+D_{ij})\}\) is nonnegative.
chunks.EstimatorBounds.stream_fee/3: Split into the coarse case \(k\le a\) and the fine case \(k>a\).
chunks.EstimatorBounds.stream_fee/4: In the coarse case \(k\le a\) the bound holds with \(\sigma=2^{a-k}\).
chunks.EstimatorBounds.stream_fee/4/3: On the source and endpoint domains, \(\min\{1,|v_{ij}|/(1+D_{ij})\}\le A|e_{ij}|\).
chunks.EstimatorBounds.stream_fee/4/3/0: Indices in the domains lie in \(S\).
chunks.EstimatorBounds.stream_fee/4/3/1: The clipped error equals its absolute value.
chunks.EstimatorBounds.stream_fee/4/3/2: For coarse bins the importance factor is \(p^4\), so \(\bar h_{ij}=p^4\,\mathbb E[h]_{ij}\) for every \(h\).
chunks.EstimatorBounds.stream_fee/4/3/6: Rewrite \(v_{ij}\) and this hypothesis using \(\bar h=p^4\,\mathbb E[h]\).
chunks.EstimatorBounds.stream_fee/4/3/8: The relative-loss bound gives at most \(32K\,|(p^4\mathbb E f)^{1/4}-(p^4\mathbb E g)^{1/4}|=32Kp\,|e_{ij}|\).
chunks.EstimatorBounds.stream_fee/4/4: By monotonicity and homogeneity of the norm, the left side is at most \(A\,\|e\|_{u,a;4}\).
chunks.EstimatorBounds.stream_fee/4/5: Narrowing to scale \(a\) leaves the axis unchanged.
chunks.EstimatorBounds.stream_fee/4/6: So the target norm is the original \(\|\cdot\|_{u,a;4}\).
chunks.EstimatorBounds.stream_fee/8: By the conditioning change and \(\rho_k/\rho_a=p^4\), \(v_{ij}=p^4\,\mathbb E[f-g\mid\mathcal C^{u,k}]_{ij}\).
chunks.EstimatorBounds.stream_fee/10/0: Indices in the domains lie in \(S\).
chunks.EstimatorBounds.stream_fee/10/2: The clipped error is at most \(|v_{ij}|/(1+D_{ij})\).
chunks.EstimatorBounds.stream_fee/11: Hence the left side is at most \(p^4\,\|A\|_{u,a;4}\).
chunks.EstimatorBounds.stream_fee/13: The ordinary difference is controlled by the root difference: \(\|f-g\|_{u,k;4}\le4K^3\|f^{1/4}-g^{1/4}\|_{u,k;4}\).
chunks.EstimatorBounds.stream_fee/14: Restate the Jensen bound for the deterministic array \(A\).
chunks.EstimatorBounds.stream_fee/16: Changing the endpoint domain from \(Y_a\) to \(Y_k\) costs \(2\cdot2^{k-a}\), so the left side is at most \(p^4\cdot2\cdot2^{k-a}\cdot4K^3\|f^{1/4}-g^{1/4}\|_{u,k;4}\), and here \(\sigma=p^3\).
chunks.EstimatorBounds.stream_fee/22: The left side equals \(8K^3p^3w\cdot(p\,2^{k-a})\) and is at most \(64K^4p^3w\).

decls.name: unit_change
decls.informal: If \(a\le a'\) and \(2^{a'}\le n\), then every deterministic array \(f\) satisfies \(\|f\|_{u,a;4}\le2\cdot2^{a'-a}\,\|f\|_{u,a';4}\).

chunks.EstimatorBounds.unit_change/2: Raising to the fourth power and swapping the endpoint scale of a deterministic array, the claim follows from \(\pi_a\le\pi_{a'}K^4\).

results.informal: A deterministic array with entries in \([0,K\rho_{a+m}]\) and row sums at most \(K\) has \(\|X_0/\rho_a\|_{u,a;4}\le4K\,2^{-3m}\).
results.note: With \(b=\rho_{a+m}\), \(2^{-3m}=(b/a)^{3/4}=(b/a)^{(s-1)/s}\) for \(s=4\), and the hypotheses are the entry bound \(Cb\) and bounded row mass used in the paper's proof (docstring: one collective loss of a wholly fine tail).

decls.name: fine_tail
decls.informal: Assume \(K\ge1\), \(2^a\le n\), \(2^u\le n\), \(|S|\le N\), \(0\le X_0(i,j)\le K\rho_{a+m}\) and \(\sum_jX_0(i,j)\le K\) for \(i,j\in S\); then \(\|X_0/\rho_a\|_{u,a;4}\le4K\,2^{-3m}\).

chunks.EstimatorBounds.fine_tail/8: It suffices to bound the fourth power of the norm by \((4K\alpha^3)^4\), and for a deterministic array it equals \(\frac1{N\rho_u}\sum_{i,j}\pi_u\pi_aT_{ij}\).
chunks.EstimatorBounds.fine_tail/12: Summing over rows bounds the norm power by \((N\rho_u)^{-1}|S|(4K\alpha^3)^4g\).
chunks.EstimatorBounds.fine_tail/14: If \(N=0\), the scale factor vanishes and the bound is trivial.
chunks.EstimatorBounds.fine_tail/19: Since \(|S|\le N\), the bound is at most \((4K\alpha^3)^4\).

results.informal: The group-\(i\) portion of walked increments equals the sum of signed, walk-weighted values over the immediate candidates, plus the base term in the first group, and every candidate descriptor has bit length at most \(4^7\cdot\text{passport}\cdot d_i\).
results.note: humid is the exact-endpoint-grouping identity for the path enumeration and lengthC the \(O(d)\)-bit description bound; the midpoint-pairing and budget clauses are not stated in these lemmas.

decls.name: humid
decls.informal: For every group \(i\), environment \(u\) and pair \((x,y)\), \(\text{portion}_i(u,x,y)=\sum_{j\in\text{tracks}(i)}\text{wind}_j(u,x,y)+[i=0]\,\text{base}(x,y)\), where \(\text{wind}_j\) is \(\pm w^h\) times the budget-\((m+1)\) or budget-\(m\) term at the endpoint of the path of \(j\) if that path is live, and \(0\) otherwise.

chunks.IterationSchedule.humid/0: Enumerate tracks ray by ray, layer by layer and path by path, expand each walked difference \(T_{m+1}-T_m\) as a sum over live paths, and match the terms.
chunks.IterationSchedule.humid/1: In the live case the terms agree, with sign \(+\) for budget \(m+1\) and \(-\) for budget \(m\).
chunks.IterationSchedule.humid/2: In the non-live case both terms are \(0\).

decls.name: lengthC
decls.informal: If \(\lambda=\ell\), \(i<L\), every ray in the forest has copy index at most \(M^2+2M+2\), \(q\) is an admissible group-\(i\) descriptor and \(p,r\le K\), then the encoding of the candidate \((q,p,r)\) has bit length at most \(4^7\cdot\text{passport}\cdot d_i\), where \(d_i\) is the slack of group \(i\).

chunks.IterationSchedule.lengthC/3: The copy index of the ray of \(q\) is at most \(M^2+2M+2\).
chunks.IterationSchedule.lengthC/4: The scale offset of \(q\) is at most \(2d\), and its slack \(\sigma\) satisfies \(d\le\sigma<2d\).
chunks.IterationSchedule.lengthC/5: The walk-event index of \(q\) has bit length at most \(cd\).
chunks.IterationSchedule.lengthC/5/2: Since \(\ell\sigma\lg\text{rad}\le cd\), the event index is below \(2^{cd}\).
chunks.IterationSchedule.lengthC/5/3: So its encoding has at most \(cd\) bits.
chunks.IterationSchedule.lengthC/6: Every number \(x\le c-1\) has bit length at most \(cd\).
chunks.IterationSchedule.lengthC/7: Every number \(x\le2d\) has bit length at most \(cd\).
chunks.IterationSchedule.lengthC/8: The scale-offset field has bit length at most \(4cd\).
chunks.IterationSchedule.lengthC/9: The copy-index and slack field has bit length at most \(4cd\).
chunks.IterationSchedule.lengthC/10: The cell of \(q\) has bit length at most \(16cd\).
chunks.IterationSchedule.lengthC/11: The first component of \(q\) has bit length at most \(64cd\).
chunks.IterationSchedule.lengthC/12: The whole descriptor \(q\) has bit length at most \(256cd\).
chunks.IterationSchedule.lengthC/13: The header \((2,p,r)\) has bit length at most \(16cd\).
chunks.IterationSchedule.lengthC/14: Pairing header and descriptor gives bit length at most \(4^7cd\).

results.informal: For a ray with accuracy guarantee coefficient \(c\), the mean prefix at the last budget \(\text{reach}(k,i)\) has clipped relative or absolute error norm at most \(c\cdot\text{wide}\cdot2^{2d_i}\cdot2^{-\lfloor|a-k|/2\rfloor}\).
results.note: This is the per-scale form of the bound \(c_*2^{-p+B_1d_j}\) with \(B_1=2\) and a geometric scale factor that is later summed over scales; wholly omitted fine scales are handled by fine_tail.

decls.name: winning
decls.informal: If the line \(f\) satisfies \(\text{Due}(s,k,d,D,b,c)\) and \(r>0\), then \(\big\|\text{toll}_b(\mathbb E[f_{\text{reach}(k,i)}]-\text{account},D)\big\|_{u,a;4}\le c\cdot\text{wide}\cdot2^{2d_i}\cdot2^{-\lfloor|a-k|/2\rfloor}\), where \(\text{toll}_b\) is the clipped relative error \(\min\{1,|\cdot|/(1+D)\}\) if \(b\) holds and the absolute error otherwise.

chunks.EstimatorBounds.winning/0: The accuracy guarantee at budget \(\text{reach}(k,i)\le M-\text{cut}(k)\) bounds the left side by \(c\,\sigma(a,k)\,\theta_{\text{reach}(k,i)}\).
chunks.EstimatorBounds.winning/2: Combining the two bounds gives the claim.

decls.name: precision
decls.informal: If \(r>0\), then \(\sigma(a,k)\,\theta_{\text{reach}(k,i)}\le\text{wide}\cdot2^{2d_i}\cdot2^{-\lfloor|a-k|/2\rfloor}\), where \(\theta_m\) is the child allowance at budget \(m\).

results.informal: The ordinary norm of a difference of carried terms is at most \(64K^4\,2^{4|a-k|}\) times the child root discrepancy, and at slack \(d\) the child allowance for both budgets \(m,m+1\) satisfies \(2^{4|a-k|}\theta_x\le\text{wide}\cdot2^{8d}\cdot2^{-\lfloor|a-k|/2\rfloor}\).
results.note: raw_fee is the unaveraged absolute comparison with scale cost \(2^{O(|h_b|)}\) and pegged converts the child accuracy into \(\text{wide}\cdot2^{8d}\), i.e. \(2^{-p-A_*+C_0d}\) with \(C_0=8\), for both parts of a paired layer; the variant-counting clause is not stated separately.

decls.name: raw_fee
decls.informal: If \(2^{\max(a,k)}\le n\), \(K\ge1\), and \(f,g\) have fourth roots in \([0,K]\) and are supported on \(Y_{\max(a,k)}\), then \(\|\text{carry}_kf-\text{carry}_kg\|_{u,a;4}\le64K^4\,2^{4|a-k|}\,\|f^{1/4}-g^{1/4}\|_{u,\max(a,k);4}\).

chunks.EstimatorBounds.raw_fee/0: Let \(c\) be the importance factor of \(\text{carry}_k\), \(a'=\max(a,k)\) and \(z=f-g\).
chunks.EstimatorBounds.raw_fee/1/1: So the mask of \(z\) is \(z\) itself.
chunks.EstimatorBounds.raw_fee/6: So the left side is at most \(c\cdot4K^3\|f^{1/4}-g^{1/4}\|_{u,a';4}\); let \(\beta=2^{4|a-k|}\).

chunks.EstimatorBounds.pegged/0: From \(m<\text{reach}(k,i)\) get \(d_i\le\text{slack}(m)\), \(\text{cut}(k)\le\text{slack}(m)\) and \(m+1<M\), and apply the raw payment bound with \(x\le M\).
chunks.EstimatorBounds.pegged/3: Its rank condition \(r>0\) is the hypothesis.

results.informal: Each walked prefix is its noise plus the conditional-mean prefix, a walk of length \(\lambda t\) shrinks noise by \(2^{-et}\), and the accumulated noise through group \(i\) is at most \(4c\cdot\text{wide}\cdot2^{-8d_i}\cdot2^{-\lfloor|a-k|/2\rfloor}\).
results.note: foggy is the noise bound of Equation (est-prefix-noise), proved through windF from the conditional-walk contraction and the raw bound pegged, runoff gives \(S_j=S_j^{\rm noise}+S_j^{\rm mean}\), and the mean bound is winning (mapped to Lemma 7.6).

decls.name: foggy
decls.informal: If \(f\) satisfies \(\text{Due}(s,k,d,D,b,c)\), \(\text{Wind}(18,\lambda)\) holds and \(r>0\), then the accumulated noise satisfies \(\|\text{noise}_{i+1}\|_{u,a;4}\le4c\cdot\text{wide}\cdot2^{-8d_i}\cdot2^{-\lfloor|a-k|/2\rfloor}\).

chunks.EstimatorBounds.foggy/0: By the triangle inequality the noise norm is at most the sum of the layer noise norms over \(m<\text{reach}(k,i)\); let \(C=2c\cdot\text{wide}\cdot2^{-8d_i}\mu\) with \(\mu=2^{-\lfloor|a-k|/2\rfloor}\).
chunks.EstimatorBounds.foggy/4/1: So \(C\), a product of nonnegative factors, is nonnegative.
chunks.EstimatorBounds.foggy/5: Each layer \(m<\text{reach}(k,i)\) has noise norm at most \(C\cdot2^{-\text{slack}(m)}\).
chunks.EstimatorBounds.foggy/5/2: The walk contraction bounds the layer noise by \(2^{-18\rho}\|f_{m+1}-f_m\|_{u,a;4}\).
chunks.EstimatorBounds.foggy/5/8: So the layer noise is at most \(2^{-18\rho}K'2^{8\rho}\).
chunks.EstimatorBounds.foggy/6: Summing the layer bounds gives at most \(C\sum_{m<\text{reach}(k,i)}2^{-\text{slack}(m)}\).
chunks.EstimatorBounds.foggy/8: Hence the noise norm is at most \(2C=4c\cdot\text{wide}\cdot2^{-8d_i}\mu\).

decls.name: windF
decls.informal: If \(16(1-\delta)^\lambda\le2^{-4e}\) and \(t>0\), then \(\|W_{\lambda t}f-\mathbb E[f\mid\mathcal C]\|_{u,a;4}\le2^{-et}\,\|f\|_{u,a;4}\), where \(W_l\) is the variant-sampling walk of length \(l\) on each conditional slice.

decls.name: runoff
decls.informal: If \(f_0=0\), then at every \((u,x,y)\), \(\sum_{m<\text{yoke}(k,i)}W_m(f_{m+1}-f_m)=\text{noise}_i+\mathbb E[f_{\text{yoke}(k,i)}\mid\mathcal C]\), where \(\text{noise}_i=\sum_{m<\text{yoke}(k,i)}(W_m-\mathbb E)(f_{m+1}-f_m)\).

chunks.EstimatorBounds.runoff/0: By induction on the number of layers, each walked increment is its noise plus \(\mathbb E[f_{m+1}]-\mathbb E[f_m]\), and the means telescope from \(\mathbb E[f_0]=0\).
